chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Wallace Post Lodge, Gino's and Buster Smith's departure
summary: A long stay in the Bronx lodge, then Gino's; Buster Smith leaves to teach in Texas.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Were you working anywhere when you had Buster Smith?
Terrace? Oh, you went back to the Queens Terrace. How do you get from the Queens Terrace to the Black House, because the Black House came up around here.
October '41 you went out on the USO shows and that probably comes to the end of the year and you're back in New York by this time.
And that's when you made these records.

Then I went up here in the Bronx, Wallace Post Lodge; a hell of a job. Joey Adams was up there; they had a different act every week but I was the local band there. I stayed there for a long time. Joey Adams was the comedian for one week. We went up there and stayed for quite
a while and then we went back downtown and went back into Gino's.
Gino's is the one on 54th Street.
And this is all when Buster Smith was in the band?
Buster stayed with you I think until he went back to Texas.
He went back to Texas to teach.
